title: Both requests run mark_paid through one runner, and bills.pay refuses the second
subtitle: Example: one electricity bill, paid from the app's chat, then again from Claude an hour later.

outcome.title: Refused: "This bill is already paid."
lines: The rule lives in bills.pay, so no entry point can skip it. The Pay button on the screen gets the same answer.

captions.title: The app's chat builds the caller's context
captions.text: A person tells Ask Billpod, the app's own assistant, that they paid the electricity bill. Before any tool runs, Ask Billpod builds one context: who asks, which household, which permissions (scopes), and that the caller is the assistant.

captions.title: A card before any change
captions.text: Gemini picks `mark_paid` from the 46 tools Ask Billpod offers. `mark_paid` is on the confirm list of 31 tools, so nothing runs yet. The person sees a card built from the stored bill and presses Approve.

captions.title: The approved call goes into the one runner
captions.text: Every AI entry point hands its calls to `runTool`. It checks the scopes and the input against the tool's schema, then runs `mark_paid`'s handler.

captions.title: The handler calls the service the Pay button calls
captions.text: The handler calls `bills.pay`, the same function the screen's REST route calls. The rules live there: the household filter and "already paid". The bill is now paid.

captions.title: An hour later, Claude calls the same tool
captions.text: The person forgot and asks Claude to pay the bill. Claude runs its own model and calls `mark_paid` over MCP with an access token. `/mcp` builds the same kind of context. Only the scopes and the caller differ.

captions.title: Here the confirmation is Claude's choice
captions.text: Billpod draws no card inside Claude. `mark_paid` carries `destructiveHint: true`, so Claude decides whether to ask first. The scopes, the input check and the service's rules still apply.

captions.title: Same runner, same service, same refusal
captions.text: The call goes through the same `runTool` to the same `bills.pay`, and the service refuses: "This bill is already paid." Claude gets it back as `isError: true`. The Pay button would get the same answer.
